I do not know if we were struck by an object or caught in the grip of something beyond knowing, but our vessel was turned from its course and separated from the rest. I saw a glimpse of the king’s vessel on the faraway black horizon, and that was the last I ever saw of my father. 

When the Viilk Marzha at last calmed, only a handful of vessels remained. The other Pan, shaking and terrified, scoured for those left alive, and counting me amongst their number, bowed their heads and groveled. 

That weakling prince, whose patchy fur and short horns were once a constant source of humiliation, was now their king.

Renson

I shouldn’t write this down. I still can’t believe it happened. But maybe if I put it to words, I’ll see it makes sense...or ain’t true.

So, Renson came over. Unannounced. Didn’t even knock, just walked right in the door. I was in the kitchen at the time, so I didn’t know he was here until the shouting started. Renson said Jaruth stole the beastie, said he’d seen it in the northeast corridor earlier this morning—same place I usually go running—but when he went there just now, it weren’t there.

I didn’t hear what Jaruth said next, but then Renson punched him in the face! I ran out to ‘em then—to stop them...I imagine...but I was too late. Renson was on the floor, a puddle of blood around his chest, the metallic smell of rust thick in the air.

And Jaruth hovered over him, knife in his hand, glowing beastie pulsating like a beating heart. I nearly tore it from him then and there.

But Jaruth had that knife.

He tried to leave, said this town weren’t good for him. I didn’t like that none, but I bit it down and told him, hey, he didn’t do nothing wrong. Weren’t his fault Renson went down the river. Self defense is what it was. I heard the whole thing. Jaruth was innocent and didn’t need to go nowhere.

Course, that ain’t what I was thinking.

I think Renson was right. I run that corridor every day and would have today if Jaruth hadn’t been coming. Did he know that? No. No, that’s crazy. But it is his fault I didn’t find the beastie first. Why else would Jaruth hide where it came from?

By rights, that beastie’s mine.

Jaruth’s out back now, looking for stones to sink the body. I came in for some rope and to set my thoughts down, get ‘em straight.

Well. I’m straight now. Best go...help him.

All Pan know of the Eafir, the song of the world. But I tell you there is a far greater song, one that hums in the space between places.

This song has power not unlike the magicks of the Laemir, but whereas the Laemir's tricks are pure spectacle, a borrowed power from the glowing stones—THIS magick is unbound. The very magick of making.

The power to give life to the lifeless!  Who would forsake that? Not to re-bind the flesh of those who once lived—not the tricks of the Laemir—but true life to that which never was.

554A94ED4C39ABF3AB7276BF93F8B751:
The Living Chronicles of the Ta’noath Clan
Generation the 1st
Trial of the Dark Sea

King Kolket knew our journey across the Dark Sea would be of great difficulty. Prince Thalos—now our king—said the same when we first set foot on these shores. How right they were. There was only nothingness here. No roofs to shelter us from the ruthless elements or beds to comfort us at night. The younglings drifted into fitful dreams in the arms of their mothers, crying weakly from the cold. Those who survived owe everything to King Thalos. He carved for us a living out of the very ground itself, with the might of his will. The young prince was cherished for his kind and gentle ways, but little did we know what a fine king he would grow into.
7E2E1C104040AA0734069EBED5D2639A:
The Living Chronicles of the Ta’noath Clan
Generation the 2nd
Trial of the Plague

Father fell to the plague, and so the fate of this family chronicle has fallen to me. Yet I have nothing happy to write about, nor much time left to write it. A chill has taken hold, causing my fur to stand on end. I feel weak, and I cannot stop shivering. I have spent these past few moons visiting the sick, trying to bring comfort to their horrid, wretched forms, which hack and convulse as their kin weep silently nearby. Their anguished faces haunt my sleepless nights. And now the sickness has claimed me as well. I know full well how this will go. First, the chills. Then the fever. Then the cough. And then... No, it is too horrible to consider. After that, I will be nothing but a mass of writhing flesh waiting to return to the soil. Not even our own soil... We are so far from home.
3F64A9484DD8FFFEB1CC558A5C654987:
The Living Chronicles of the Ta’noath Clan
Generation the 3rd
A Glimpse of the Clan’s Future

I can contain my joy no longer: I am with child! This will be the first youngling born to me! We feared it would not be possible after such terrible sickness. Such agony and death. It seems not long ago I felt so weak I could not even lift my head.

The Vaunnts gifted me a living stone to help me while my beloved attends the king. It is hard to believe this thing will raise my youngling alongside me. I have not yet thought of a name.

For the living stone, of course! For the little one, we have long decided upon the name Ra’len’ell-zare’ta’noath for a girl and Akar for a boy. Such perfect, beautiful names!
C8981F324032937F1B1BB7AAC0AC94D5:
The Living Chronicles of the Ta’noath Clan
Generation the 4th
The Story of Me

I did it! I swiped the important book from mother’s belongings, and now I will write my mem... Memory? No, that’s not it. I can’t remember the word. But I will write the story of me, Ra’len of the Ta’noath clan!

What do I like to do? I like to dance, and even more, to sing. Sometimes I sneak out with G’ar, my stone friend, and I dance and dance to the joyful notes of its song. It’s such a nice song. The others don’t hear it too well, but that’s okay. I can hear it, and it makes me happy.
1F8B215345838B6B577AC990B162CEEA:
The Living Stones

Let it be known that Ro’thinderahenwalt was right! I always believed in the living stones. The ridicule I endured... Ah, but that’s all over. I will return triumphant, with an army of stones at my command. The empress will tremble in fear! They will build a statue in my honor! A giant one, with the help of my stones! Ah, no, enough. One step at a time. There is still much to figure out. How did Lydusa control the stones? How?! And the question that turns my stomach remains unanswered... Where is my tribe now? Hm. I will have my answers, and my Pan will have their freedom. That will make all I’ve done to get here worth it.

There was once a doe who lived deep within the jungle. She was larger than any of her ilk, with dappled white fur and antlers that scraped the clouds. She could leap as high as the kuri kuri, and she was strong and proud. 

For many long nights, our hunters sought to fell the doe, but in her ancient, wild grace, she deftly dodged their spears and avoided their arrows. No Pan could catch her, or so we thought.

Then one day, a young maiden sat alone in the forest and began to sing. Her sweet voice carried on the wind, and the doe, enchanted by the sound, descended from the floating isles and rested her head on the maiden’s lap. 

The maiden wept as the hunters descended, for only in that moment did she realize the cruelty of her trick. But the proud doe did not flinch or tremble, not even as the hunters surrounded her and impaled her with spears. 

The doe said to the maiden, “Do not cry for me. To catch me, you became clever. To kill me, you became strong. And now, I will feed your bellies so that you become healthy. One day, you too will feel the spears of death, and all your cleverness, strength, and vitality will return to my jungle. Your horns will sprout into branches, your fur will bud into leaves, your voice will bloom into flowers; and you will feed the bellies of my fawns.” 

The maiden never forgot the doe’s lesson that day, and she carved this statue in her memory. When the maiden grew elderly, she insisted her body not be interred in the crypts, but near this statue instead. Her final sigh was one of peace, for she knew her death would not be in vain.

When will our king return? This question echoes across our shadowed ziggurats, at once a prayer and a muted accusation. He has been gone for very nearly a year, and in that time, so many of his people have fallen prey to the illness that has followed the Pan from shore to shore like a specter. There are whispers that King Thalos fell to this same sickness and that his death is being kept from us, as the promise of his light is the only trace of hope that remains. But we refuse to believe that. It cannot be true! He is out there, and he will return, salvation in hand. Ah, but will there be anyone left to witness his triumph?

My sweet daughter, you are very nearly grown, and I pray you live long enough to have younglings of your own, though I fear I will never meet them. I am weak... So weak. I must lay down my head and rest, just for a moment.

Where do I begin? It has been my life’s pursuit to bring ink to paper, and yet I am at a loss.

Facts. I’ll begin with the facts. And that means I must begin with the plague.

Kolket was on the throne, his enemies in their graves. Coin, drink, and good times were available to all his subjects.

Then one day, rumors begin to circulate of Pan falling sick in the outskirts of Ang-Forehn. Overnight, shops and guilds in major settlements begin to shutter. Before we know it, everyone knows someone who knows someone who died. There are whispers that this blood is all paid to Fate—the price of Kolket’s many wars—the bill due for his victorious body count.

Weeks later we all know death. We all know one who is the last of his line. We are the lucky ones, they say, but there’s no end in sight. The world is poison to us now. And that’s when Kolket tells us of the ships.

No one who has sailed beyond the horizon has returned from the Dark Sea. Fools call it the edge of the world—a concept that seems ridiculous, for would not all the water rush off the edge of the table? But for all we know they’re right.

Yet we cannot stay here.

At last, I know what it is I am writing. A chronicle of the last voyage of the Pan.

E1B6DE274D8CC6045C32F69EA065C7DD: “Across the great expanse of history, it has been proven time and again that speed is as integral to victory as might, though when joined, the two traits become immeasurably more fearsome. 1872C5CC4001D58E453791B0F98BBC64: “I am what you might call an ardent collector of rare and valuable items. Whether their worth is derived from their composition, their prior owner’s prominence, or their intended secrecy, I make it my business to find and hoard such prizes. After all, you never know when such a thing will prove beneficial.”
021B05EC4604D0EDC83FC79E13DFA571: “I can scarcely tolerate lowering myself to wear such rags in the name of self-preservation, but must they be so tattered as to reveal glimpses of a fugitive Fae’s wings?! One truly cannot trust the Dran to adequately accomplish anything!”
1EB8AE9C44B3312FC863EB9661E9795C: “I can tell just by looking at it that it's from Corsus. That place where its inhabitants have fully embraced the 'Iskal'. The fact that it's made from an eye much larger than any human's only adds to its gruesome nature.”
462EF0F44674B28563CDFD9FB37995DC: “I confess, we Fae are fond of things that sparkle. A glittering coin, a fanciful gemstone... Whatever it’s made from is far less important than the intensity of its gleam, surely you agree. Come now, it doesn’t really matter, does it? It looks so lovely on you.”
477E595B4972E373527C75BDC2C29F41: “I could happily live the rest of my days without ever again glimpsing the horrific creations that the Dran attempt to pass off as art. Unrefined, unnerving, and wholly without merit, every last piece!”
250B153F4727F0E78295169C7D58553E:
“I do not aim with my hand; he who aims with his hand has forgotten the face of his father.
I aim with my eye."
D639FBD5445B65D558EF78B5FBD9D577: “I have heard tale of those who were driven mad by an inescapable nightmare in which they wander endlessly before coming upon a world of death and decay. In the midst of this world, they find only an empty throne, consecrated in blood. These are...merely the ravings of a scant few feeble-minded Dran, of course. Even still, I sleep with a razor-sharp quill beneath my pillow, just in case.”
7FC1100A459B04A33A0EF0818E5EC125: “I have little to offer, but the Paxultek’s need is no doubt greater than mine. Let it take whatever aids its path. Only leave a token for the Balance.”
9ACD80E54B82195A0A58149C4AD90FB8: “I inherited this seal from my predecessor. The previous Royal Scribe was tragically terminated from his position after earning the ire of the king’s mistress. His downfall was my ascension, and I am far too sagacious to repeat such foolhardy mistakes.”
527266634009B598E85999B37D26D2C1: “I once served as an archivist in the royal library. There I was most content, lost in the forbidden tomes and secrets of eld... Including those the king dared not reveal to the Fae. Such was my misfortunate undoing as an archivist, and my beginning as his scribe.”
642FC1FF4BE78F6F7B7B7FBB24C0196F: “I swear, if they ask me to cut orange slices again, it’ll be more than oranges that I end up cutting. I am too damn busy for shit like this.”
1250C223445F6F58E4DB03833177E7E5: “I usually don't mind trading war stories or talking about how the Mud Dogs landed a big score, but how I came upon these, I'm gonna take that with me to my grave.”
33CA70E440717D2104391FAB764502B1: “I'm quite familiar with Lumenite, but this corrupted version is new to me. The fact that it exists is concerning and could mean trouble ahead."
775174C1413DAF3E74F7B8912D909F6A: “If Rhom has one legacy, that’d be the stunning misuse of power. In a world where the few survivors struggled to endure unlivable conditions and their own brutal mutations, somewhere in the shadows this twisted science project of death was also created. Damn them all.”
F258C19A44D114B16A1F3391413DD9E6: “If certain creatures notice you, you’re as good as dead. In their presence, the snap of a twig can easily lead to the snap of a neck.”
1AC1A0C4494BC60379BE1A84823398F5: “If there is civilization, then there is artistry. Some believe the two must coexist. If one crumbles then the other is soon to follow.”
DDA0F7394FAC5D8CB1C236A003ACE9FC: “If you ever catch sight of cold steel and a colder gaze aimed at you from beneath a wide-brim hat, it’s time to make your peace.”
4946E5D3410F43719CC2ACAB6251246B: “If you're unable to be inventive, your survival prospects are grim at best. It's time to put that eccentric notion you've been saving into action.”
E86D7EA74DDB1C960EA202BEE26DEAD8: “Impalement is Bruin’s preferred method of torture. Why, you ask? Excruciating pain aside, it is a terrible indignity for your lifeless corpse to adorn the palace walls like a bauble to be gawked at. I would much rather perish somewhere furtive and forgotten, like a cozy alleyway or a shallow ditch. Far less humiliating.”
9755AB1045F356ED2629FB972A88B990: “In a world of living nightmares, you think of a hero as the person with the shiny blade spilling blood and slicing up monsters. Don’t ever forget that it takes a certain brand of bravery to go back for the wounded and challenge death itself.”
A3ECF1954FA9857E3AA2698522F2A035: “In perusing a prior scribe’s memoirs, I came upon an entry about a certain young princeling crying his eyes out for weeks on end over the sudden loss of his mother, the only soul who harbored any love for the child. This insight into the Red Prince’s fear of loss and secret longing to be cared for has proven most valuable.”
7DB8C01A4F8026A8996BB2AED000E74E: “In their search for other forms of life, the Drzyr were not blind to the fact that any such entities had a relatively high probability of being hostile. They were not naïve to this possibility, nor were they unprepared.”
B0AC37F34EF9EFF9D2FB28B21DEB407A: “In these times of desperation, the only way to survive is for the hunted to become the hunter. Otherwise, the flickering flame of humanity will be extinguished once and for all.”
A0BDF58E410BE38A28B4168F707C6F16: “In these times of political upheaval and rampant vengeance, a clever disguise is perhaps more integral to survival than a sharpened blade. After all, the latter will only get you killed, while the former allows one to move amongst the shadows until an opportune time for reemergence presents itself.”
4A6EE4C242A55908CE9416820B9FA0EC: “In truly dire times, you’ve got to get back to your roots—no pun intended! A lot of weapons we use today, even the deadliest, are made from sticks and stones and whatever else we can find.”
1D9343F64FD8032EAB42B88B48E5E50A: “Input forms the foundation of an artificial intelligence’s existence, an indispensable resource that ensures its ongoing evolution. The more data it absorbs, the more refined and precise its operations become. Deprive it of that input, and its systems would falter, unable to sustain the intricate functions required to operate.”
4233701D4BEE49B7222C3E9138E5B94D: “Is there nothing more comforting / than the silence of the end / that deep, irreparable void / of what could once be?”
18533D1549A35057B90468B46E565A82: “It is said that King Kolket left no heir, but every Pan youngling grew up hearing legends of a long-lost prince who went missing during their dangerous voyage across the Dark Sea. Tragically, many young, tenderhoofed explorers met untimely demises searching for proof of his existence.”
7176A7A44B3BF8361A0A76AD7DBE3F3F: “It is said that King Thalos was beloved by his Pan, even as a prince back in our original homeland. It is an abomination that he came to be known as the Bloodless King due to the machinations of the stone goddess. Yet the Pan need never know of his descent... No, indeed. Some secrets are best left buried, so as not to dull the brilliance of the legends that give us the strength to carry on.”
BCD7BEED48C2F52B35666D84331675A4: “It is utterly absurd to believe farfetched tales about an object that can whisk one away to an ethereal coast wholly separate from reality! Who is capable of conjuring such a thing, and to what end? For what toll? Questions like these leave a foul taste in my mouth, and yet...I find it difficult to lay aside my fascination with the thought of possessing such a rare treasure.”
D0BC06734B2E32AEAEC5EA9E9EDBC18B: “It may not be the most fashionable gear, but if these goggles keep your eyes protected when things get rough, it's more than worth it."
151C59EF4E45D2F38FDFFC838E3D299B: “It might be a flesh prison, but it’s your one and only flesh prison. Take good care of it.”
D7564F2D470D03F08CA3478C79E41DD7: “It takes more than tonics and herbs to heal a broken world, there’s no arguing with that—but damned if they ain’t a start.”
522E842745457AB1B5B88580B59D3C1A: “It's strange how every artifact the Wanderer retrieved from Reisum exudes an unmistakable chill, as if they were still imbued with the frost of the land."
A17704384F30CD71020421B53550185B: “It’s a terrible torment to be the sole bearer of the king’s secrets. I have to wonder if such cruelty was the king’s intent in making me his scribe. To know his every last confession and musing, yet be forever sworn to excrutiating confidentiality... He may as well have tortured me with a blade.”
3481CD3E4E238145E5B537BAD4CEDE8D: “It’s funny how something as trivial as a cloth cap can call to mind more innocent times. In these dark days, that’s arguably more vital than a solid defense.”
9A5D1B3C4BB3F38F46A6569574CA28B7: “It’s one thing to go after enemies on a battlefield. In times of war, a healer is a soldier who must also outwit the enemies within.”
3E6A530346F05D440A0D52BA2C38641C: “I’ll take your scrap, sure. Just don’t expect a “friend discount” or anything dumb like that. You owe me enough already.”
ACD0DE8B4EF514C90DD33F8D5611EDBA: “I’ve got better things to do than cobble together meaningless prizes to cushion some random traveler’s bruised ego. Keep it. Toss it. Eat it, for all I care. Just stay the hell away from me if you know what’s good for you.”
7DB5400C41F77982502B3EB5CC9EFC82: “I’ve heard tale of a band of Dran occultists who operate in the shadows and distinguish each other by means of dark symbology. As a master of surfacing that which others mean to keep buried, I am of course aware of said symbology, and I use this knowledge to stay as far away from those rabid ritualists as my feet can carry me.”
F41A6ADE4CB38E3D6142E3947BACD733: “I’ve seen a fair number of worlds in my time, and there’s one thing they all have in common—sometimes it only takes the smallest flicker light to bring hope to the darkest times.”
72C9864D414E441A4F60D5AEA0D1832E: “Just as the Dran, the pigs, and the birds are simply pitiable creatures to those of us with higher-born blood, so too are even the Fae to monsters of legend such as the Sunken Witch. Do I believe these stories, decidedly unproven and without evidence? Of course not! Yet will you find me venturing near the shores after dark? You absolutely never will.”
D65A09B646AF2DD278865388E06EFA28: “Just because those bookish types are smart doesn’t mean they know nothin’. Some of the best thinking comes from the commonfolk, but because they can’t spell or count right, nobody cares to listen.”
1A86CC0C4D53D28E3C193C91D27F916B: “Just like a discarded tire fashioned into makeshift armor, for certain stalwart individuals, their service never ends—it simply evolves.”
B7C0F3E74E18F5EA653EDDA8C52CBA01: “Legend has it that the Sunken Witch has a number of calling cards. First, a mirthless laugh that is often the last thing her victims hear. Second, an anchor she acquired from a ship after bludgeoning its crew to death. Lastly, a complete lack of mercy, which is why there are only legends rather than firsthand accounts of the sea witch.”
5028778B4304C64C35C48AAC9EB9D1E1: “Like a firefighter running towards the flame, scientists don’t run from an impossible problem. They face it head on, even at the risk of life and limb. They’ll never back down until they’ve achieved the understanding they seek, ‘cause for folks like them, that’s the ultimate victory.”
E5593FED41DE8996F6C2019CD5A6E489: “Look upon the fruits of grief / grown in shallow waters and soil dry / and mourn their dreadful ripenings.”
0787474D45ED0FAA126660A62D1C8552: “Malicious intent is usually masked behind a façade of beauty, necessity, or perhaps simple distraction. The Dran, however, are a curious sort. Their little toys and machinations make no attempt to hide their cruel intentions.”
DBD96E804F656278E5E35ABBF3F2CAE0: “Many of the materials used to build N’Erud were harvested from other planets, moons, and asteroids. Reassurance: the Seekers would never requisition materials from a planet on which living beings exist. This alloy is an innocuous sample intended for study.”
C8E0003D410F169E5663DEA843702944: “Mariner, oh mariner / lost upon the ice-capped sea / alone and frightened.”
59B34132484A587507A2E38DC0DDEA0E: “Miserable, loathsome creatures that exist merely as a spectacle of misery for the rest of us to watch in horror and pity from a great distance. That is all the Dran are, from birth to death, and all they might ever strive to be.”
0BB673114FD6425436BCBCA4E67A836F: “Much can be hidden beneath the veil of the ocean’s creeping mists, unbeknownst to the countless simpletons who willfully turn away from such occulted knowledge. This is perhaps how the rise of ritualism proliferated so readily across the Dran docks.”
AC5FFC804688B4C6A4968B8E8628A6E3: “No matter what gets you down, dear, make sure you always look right presentable. Tie your cravat nice and neat every morn, and the rest of the day will follow its lead.”
36CA40754E2A2A92D56D92A9AE462643: “Not as good as my ward-renowned stew, but this stuff’ll do in a pinch…as long as you ain’t expecting to feel the same way twice!”
62F768AE4DA1682DA8937AAD9B7EA08A: “Not even the studied magisters understood the sorcery that bound these knights to the king’s mistress. That the knights were more than willing to serve the lady consort in life and death suggests she earned affections beyond those of her king. Doesn’t it?”
831AB0174C9620F93247D6BC138C551B: “N’Erud demands unceasing vigilance to ensure the smooth operation of even its most basic infrastructure. To move the vast quantities of agricultural goods across the planet, all 989 rail loader systems must remain operational at all times.”
4AFD7536483DD554BE7D12A942CE507B: “N’Erud was created as a haven for the civilization that inhabited it. Like any such place, it was not without its secrets, hidden amid labyrinthine paths and safe from the prying eyes of patrolling machinery and the uninitiated.”
84944038489E1DD07C9CF1ADF431BF1E: “Oh, no, no, no. I never indulge in such things. Shaedberry wine has a way of loosening the tongue, and loosened tongues are quickly severed in these lands. Many Fae have met their shameful, hastened end by consequence of indulgence.”
996710F84FED7183BAB9BA9FD7092D51: “Ol’ Mudtooth has gone a-wanderin’ ‘round every corner of this here big, blue marble, and I tell ya, I still ain’t never seen a hat no fancier than this un! You plop this beaut on yer noggin and you’ll be a gen-u-wine cassee-nova! Hehehe!”
7A4EB87549908ACE22D915A3195DC79B: “Only short-sighted halfwits put their machinations readily to ink. Truly sagacious Fae keep their most precious secrets, penned or otherwise, sequestered far beyond where prying eyes dare to peek.”
0FF8243447FAF5E12165D2B6647DAA84: “Only these drab Dran creatures are imbecile enough to choose a life of solitude on the damp, dusky shores over the intrigue of civilized company. I say, leave them to their tides and their legends! The moment the chance arrives, I shall abandon this miserable drudgery and return to the decadence that I so richly deserve.”
2F3B553E4208B2D8BE3A849ACA4A0CA9: “Or perish in the abandon, the sweet abysmal end; / Departed, waylaid, dead!”
5CEE7F26442B6078CD286DADBA194D92: “Out in the war-torn wilds where it’s a battle just to scrape out a living, you’ll quickly find that functionality is key and frills are for the foolhardy.”
DC85D43740D1C8623630E39C3358E89C: “Perception is the only difference between concepts such as good and evil, right and wrong, and so on and so forth. The ability to shift your perspective just so in a way that allows you to dance between these extremes as needed is the true art of the Fae.”
155706054BAA0AB8B9CFE9A82C336D3E: “Perish in the abandon, the sweet abysmal end...”
ED7B36C540273918F2E9AB853986804B: “Please follow all safety procedures while in possession of the extractor. Do not point the extractor in the direction of another living being. Do not insert any appendages into the extractor. Caution: if the extractor is used for any purpose other than alloy collection, House Lythla will be notified.”
173474BC41F144FE0B203581E2E90847: “Raw potential. A formless, seething mass from which all things were made in the small hours of the worlds. So rare that only a handful of people have even heard of it, let alone laid their eyes upon it.”
C62B931046254598F5D3F9A9A7D541BE: “Really, why in the world do you have that repulsive thing? It’s utterly horrendous. I...I think I’m going to gag. Please take it—and yourself—far, far away from me!”
1975333046F706FBFB9FEDA11DD5587B: “Renegades, rebels, resistors... Call them what you want. Every world’s got 'em, and in my experience, it’s worth hearing them out. Most of the time, they understand the world around them better than the ones in charge.”

6215D36848577B10EE29DCBA7E301A7A: “Royalty is an alien concept to the Drzyr. Although certain houses exert more influence than others, they are not worshipped. Within the houses themselves, experts of their house’s unique discipline are often the most respected and called upon.”
A798B4374B21E04C73C3CB8B8D9FA3A0: “Self-sacrifice and cooperation were mandated principles for members of the lower houses. Through periods of discontent and even rebellion, these inborn ideals sustained their general solidarity enough to ensure eventual acquiescence in favor of the greater good.”
9D6CCAF34E6AC081F418F98A5B0D1E95: “Sentience exists to be corrupted. To submit in totality to defilement and putrefaction, to be sundered of its discordant wholeness and recast anew for our endmost design.”

9041EBDB496B200F0A47BFB8D56698F6: “Since the beginning of the Drzyr civilization, the Drzyr held forums to determine the future of their species. 8696CD2C4A8A7F8FD0B2849E3D0B96DC: “Stronger even than iron and steel is the bond between man and beast. After all, if you fall in battle, your gun won’t keep fighting on your behalf, but a loyal sidekick will.”
35EB256C4FC75BB42E28F69213739B97: “Tal’Ratha was the Primis Astropath of House Wek. He was highly regarded as a brilliant and respectable mind, and he and I were often called upon by the Convocation. 5B699CB04D726DB874FB3DA80829A369: “That the One True King suffered the young prince to live despite his attempted coup is a curious thing. Either the king thought exile a punishment graver than death...or his mercy bespoke that which he dared not otherwise admit.”
84052B9B476D80E30950D08C23658663: “The Agronomy Sector is one of the largest sectors aboard N’Erud. In order for the Ofildi to effectively and quickly cross its surface, the Xul developed the D.H. Transit Drone. Efficiency saw a significant increase, as did serious injuries. Thus the Seekers instituted unique glyphs so that only properly certified Ofildi could operate the drones.”
8DF94FD243A0367B1CA1AFBA71C5C435: “The Ahanae are masters of the arcane arts, and it is they alone who are capable of manipulating the magical energies infused within the crystals found throughout our jungles. 7F042640403E6115CA75AC967A8892E9: “The Blood Moon heralds death, as does the pestilence. One warns the Pan of our end, and the other brings it.”
99F4601F44BC30A9205EC1BDCEBA1D24: “The Dran live their menial lives at the sea’s behest, tromping through dank sewers and damp docks like the vermin they are. To walk a mile in their dismal shoes is more than enough to demonstrate the good fortune there is in being born a Fae...though I daresay only a few steps would have sufficed.”
AFE190EB44D93D1862DAD4B4947939C2: “The Dran ritualists are known for making full use of their victims even well after their demise. Though tortuously deprived of life, they should count themselves lucky that they are already dead when it comes time to harvest their bones and entrails. Well...usually.”
35C9F6224AF3E210DE85A3A00B288F9D: “The Drzyr could not survive without machines. Their way of life depended upon us to uphold it. We were expendable, able to be remade and repaired again and again to suit the needs of the Drzyr. This solemn service, we would offer to our creators without question.”
FB7D9C2B498C7049BB34A5AEF22AA143: “The Drzyr legacy must endure. If we are truly the only sentient life in this dark, empty expanse, then our species must be preserved no matter the cost. The ambit ember has revealed this to be my destiny. My sacrifice to bear. For I love the Drzyr, fallible as we are.”
9B00EC6D4E2134B302526BA80EA4AF38: “The Drzyr made countless attempts to petition Sha’Hala directly. I would have liked to attempt making contact myself, but the Seekers refused. It is unlikely, yet possible that Sha’Hala’s means of communication more closely resembles that of an artificial intelligence than those of my creators. Regrettably, we may never find out.”
C6DF531E4300BF33BE17FDB8CF0A0F01: “The Drzyr surrounded themselves with implements and creations that kept them always in a delicate balance between the preservation of life and an untimely death. Most became accustomed to this state, and those who did not were swiftly silenced.”
A06A23A54A82DA913F8FDBB2E5EE9FE3:
“The Drzyr were a self-perpetuating civilization, and N’Erud itself a self-sustaining cradle of life. It could withstand forces greater than those that ravaged our home planet. Greater than any force in the universe. 

So, we thought.”
EB4151EC4671FD2EC501E2B443543BD6: “The Fae are so often accused of vanity, but is it truly a crime if such a wealth of pride is warranted, earned, and utterly irrefutable? I, for one, would take sweet vanity and the whispers it elicits over morose mediocrity any day!”
E09B8378411BD5CF3F7A8181AB858F41: “The Nymphs understand the Kin-Mother better than Pan and pestilence both. They bend all of nature to their capricious will, and they do not forgive those who defile their blessings.”
6BF480F64C06A85B8FB26B83A3BC1169: “The One True King has many secrets hidden within the dark recesses of his castle, and it would seem, the blackened organ he calls a heart. Such secrets, of course, are ripe for the picking, begging those clever enough to spy them to uncover such treasures and await the opportune moment to bring them to light.”
68CFA2104D5F6B58AA16E6B9D65E90BB: “The One True King is rarely moved to engage in battle, rather preferring to end things quickly, or better yet, with excruciating slowness upon a fresh pike. You must have really and truly gotten under his skin. Bravo, my friend! Never fail to remember that I was cheering you on from afar and celebrated your achievement most jubilantly.”
641822BA4F891CD0C3598A90C7F325C4: “The Phetyr held that true warriors were never defenseless. Even without a traditional weapon, they were always poised to prevail in any encounter.”
9641A89645A11865769D528A13A29948: “The Phetyr thrived on competition, even in weapon design. The Genesis Bow, facing a formidable rival, distinguished itself with one standout feature: 32x Blast Processing, as its creator was quick to point out.”
906ED8C3456E9A73BE850AB51196C60B: “The Red Doe has long been revered as a blessed symbol for the Pan. A portent of the end of hardship and the beginning of a new journey for our kind. What, then, shall become of those corrupted souls who would harm such a pure being for their own prosperity?”
01FFDBAC430D23050A1AE79B3DFF0B08: “The Red Prince may just as suitably have been dubbed Red Death, for along his meandering march to the throne, he leaves a trail of crimson blood in his path. All for the glory and good of the Fae, there can be no doubt. The only thing he lacks is an ever-loyal scribe to render immortal his many accomplishments...”
F0BF356E452857327DC359B4E86AD01F: “The Root never left us any time for sentimentality. I don’t care if the darn thing’s saved your life countless times—when you find something better, you’ve gotta take it. And don’t you dare look back.”
B7D9700D457C80B703A9C79F364041FF: “The Root only understand pain. To make it in this twisted world of theirs, one must become fluent in that language.”
1D51565642F22F2899973AB348151F84: “The Wanderer used to wear this ring. Not sure if it was special somehow, or if they just liked how it looked. Ha... Can’t say I ever understood what was going on in that mind of theirs!”
0B9204304B7F197F477FDC94604CABB1: “The Wasting, a fabled plague that ravaged Fae-kind as divine retribution for our nefarious misdeeds. Please, only a proper fool would believe the king’s carefully weaved fictions. But such fools are the masses made of, I suppose!”
1BEE7E774BFBA1462549D8A3163BF2D0: “The beauty of the supernovae / rent in twain, collapsed again / the cosmic goodbye.”
EACE344749F757B4FAB5EDA605B2F757: “The biggest mistake you can make while exploring the unknown is to underestimate your enemy—but that goes both ways. I don’t care how many horns or wings or whatever a foe may be packing, if they see this shovel and think the odds are in their favor, you’re in a prime position to make sure that’s the last thought they ever have.”
7C1A07F2444DD1C45A7151A6A6134CF2: “The comets dash the firmament / inviting us to play!”
FA48276F47B81ED81CA13592C5867130: “The concept of salvation from nothingness is a result of flawed logic. Nothingness is the salvation, life is the corruption, and we are the cure for the afflicted.”
CD4103B04499D0E8EEB958B0DD8AA019: “The councilors gracelessly served no master but themselves, and their ill-plotted coup was doomed from its conception. Perhaps if they had made room for a properly brilliant, astute tactician to guide their slavering whims, they might have succeeded. Alas. I’ll not shed a tear for them.”
10CF3A3E406ADBAE38C4AD84EABF8465: “The culmination of everything the Drzyr had worked for over the course of countless generations came down to a single second. Time stood still, and in that endless moment, the fate of Drzyr civilization was forever altered.”
0AA48E1B4D8CB6F50332AF89BE1877BB: “The currency of the Dran is blood and sorrow, and for those willing to pay, there is much to be gained. I am not personally an enthusiast of self-inflicted pain—nor any pain aimed at myself, for that matter—but I must admit there is something endlessly fascinating about these strange and grisly customs of theirs.”
B925061B47BDDB9D262FE7B4C56724FA: “The dark clouds harken the universe’s end...”
7E3572254EB47556980024A13034245A: “The dark clouds that harken the universe’s end / part in presence of dear, beloved friend!”
BF1E556C448176526BF20EBFFC72272A: “The dockworkers inexplicably take immense pride in their work, claiming to read the sea as though it were an ancient tome of ageless wisdom. Rubbish, of course, but if it keeps them preoccupied and out of my sight, I have no cause for complaint. Yes, leave them to their legible waters! May they drown in them.”
2BAD3CD74930934254DFA48EF60B981C: “The dulls of the universe / are long and agonizing. The end, then / a thousand stars exploding / seems exciting.”
411E8C69492D16775623C88AF5FA94E2: “The fingerless leather gloves provide exceptional dexterity to the wearer, while the vambraces are adorned with a blue gem that gives the wearer access to the volatile energy stored within.”
2CCC44C0406BB992535E6E87808D0608: “The flames of the stone goddess’s fury are such that cannot ever be quelled. She is a nasty, vengeful creature! It is not possible to reason with beings who are drunken with power. Trust me on this. All one can do is conspire in secret, await the perfect timing, and then go to great lengths to avoid being consumed by the conflagration.”
72DFF2F34E0A2DAFC1DBCD834619C8B4: “The goddess Nimue was long kept as the One True King’s trusted advisor. How she earned his trust is anyone’s guess, but she was privy to even more than my own prying eyes thanks to this position. The mistake that led to her imprisonment wasn’t treachery, but merely a lack of conviction to see her traitorous plans through to the bitter end.”
451C624349EDCA7E6DD2D0935BC82FDD: “The journey of the glorious moon and her effect on kin-mother Yaesha is a subject of great interest to the Pan, most especially for Pan scholars like myself. The way she goes from emptiness to fullness to emptiness again, never doubting that what is depleted will in time be reclaimed... It fills Ro’thinderahenwalt’s heart with hope that the same might be true of his hopes and dreams.”
DBE9310649512545586C828B9C945F50: “The king is dead, and I daresay, I played no small part in that endeavor. The Fae, most particularly myself included, can now resume the normal course of life without fearing the pike or a blade in the night for any supposed betrayals of the past. In this upset of power, there is much to be gained, and no time to dally in ensuring it is my hand that is outstretched first to secure whatever prizes await.”
5EA0F1DA4BFFFF051E7432A0437123AF: “The knights were meant to protect the king’s beloved from ill-intentioned Fae envious of her lofty position—not that I make acquaintances of Fae like that—yet it’s recorded that she preferred to handle such assailants personally. One need not wonder why the king was so very fond of her."
4FBFA68C4A4027E544092BAD81BD4E26: “The knights who aided the prince in his rebellion have long since succumbed to the dregs of time, but the prince honors their names and likenesses still. And the knights who serve him now are as loyal and gallant as their forebearers—I daresay more so than any knight who ever served the One True King.”
2FCEAF734F48493B661211A12AC0A13A: “The machines and arthropods cannot comprehend the fate of our world. Of the Drzyr. Their lack of intelligence affords them precious bliss, and for that I envy them.”
A249723040A3E73EC08D7D9D31176DB3: “The mask, crafted by the Red Widows of Yaesha, serves as a haunting reminder that power can shift in an instant, depending on the tools at hand. It's a testament to the fact that those who were once healers and medicine women can become queens, elders, and even gods with the right resources.”
5EC7EAF745B19660CF5F17A675FFED2A: “The most fortuitous position one can place themselves in is to be in the good graces of a powerful being, especially one that could make miserable your existence with the wave of a hand. By favor, or best yet, by carefully executed blackmail—it matters not how you achieve such a boon, only that you preserve it at all costs.”
0F5611AA4D372AFF70710FB54D70EAD0: “The one thing the Root doesn’t have is the will to live. It’s that stubbornness, those instincts to survive, that have kept humanity going for so long.”
63A86E3743D5CEC0ACBDF1807FE14186: “The one thing the Root doesn’t have is the will to live. It’s that stubbornness, those instincts to survive, that have kept humanity going for so long.”
9EC39CDA477DD240DEABD0A90A514619: “The one thing the Root doesn’t have is the will to live. It’s that stubbornness, those instincts to survive, that have kept humanity going for so long.”
FCAC97264C18AF7F83B061BFEFC89BB2: “The prince’s mother is always depicted with her face veiled by a mask. Some claim the mask concealed harrowing battle scars, or perhaps preserved an impossibly beautiful and delicate visage. Of course, I know the truth of the matter: that the king would not dare permit his consort to ever reveal her face, not even to her son—who now obscures his own in precisely the same manner.”
9089E2964B3F5833338AADB5D2CA4C38: “The search for life beyond our own meant leaving the life we knew behind. But as the stars of our universe dimmed, so too did our resolve. For if we alone braved this universe, what would become of it once we were gone?”
78FAD0C247E5DE3648F4A387F2AD01C1: “The sinister curve of a ritualist’s blade has come to be associated with death, and for good reason. It is not only an effective means of carnage, but an appropriately frightening one that haunts the dreams of those fair few who have ever seen it and lived to tell the tale.”
EB4478D24688E6F926F705981C273CC0: “The so-called Blade of the King was plucked from the depths of our most forgotten gaol, where he was imprisoned on account of his perverse bloodlust and cruelty. Indeed, the very same vices for which the king would later elevate him to prominence.”
A31F17924186C9DAFC4B9ABB36FA96EF: “The stars on the horizon twinkle in full bloom / bright and happy!”
578F51544B819DEAF4D99AA08492277D: “The thing about ingenuity is it requires both a stroke of inspiration and the sheer force of will to bring your vision to life. Never underestimate someone who possesses this quality, and I wouldn’t recommend turning your back on them either.”
4E99240240F9DAD1AAC3E2AB637B592F: “The very genesis of the Drzyr’s long journey was the fear and despair born of the knowledge that their host star would one day burn out, extinguishing all life and hope along with it. It could be considered poetic that fearing the loss of light is what led the Drzyr to ultimate darkness.”
D983683249E7477BBC4628B8D66BF8EB: “The wisest among us, such as yours truly, know full well never to take anything at face value. Especially here, and especially now. For the moment you allow yourself to believe that you’ve attained some amount of understanding or control, the world has a way of burying each one of your hubristic misconceptions, and you along with them.”
E0FA3F4C4B197949152FAA9A20A85BC1: “The wisest among us, such as yours truly, know full well never to take anything at face value. Especially here, and especially now. For the moment you allow yourself to believe that you’ve attained some amount of understanding or control, the world has a way of burying each one of your hubristic misconceptions, and you along with them.”
B21651AF40015A5FED51EE9D7047CC06: “There are no innocents among the Fae, at least not in the One True King’s mind. He possessed a certain vision for our kind—one we by our very natures could never hope to achieve. After all, what he saw as desecrations were to us simple instincts. Even so, not even the Dran, docile as they are, were spared his condemnation.”
801EAF5647D4D6F66B74C192D6BCFC00: “There are some Fae who cannot feel the sensation of pain at all. Though I’m no devotee of agony myself, I don’t envy them one bit. Regrettably, a world without pain is far more dangerous than one otherwise. Why, come the darkness of night, I’d much rather be able to feel the blade in my back than not.”
791A6C784A6DC74719A6FE9F95B5B361: “There exists no sentient being that can avoid cessation. Every last entity will be disinterred and eradicated. Inescapable oblivion awash with silence.”
6F110DD24D398ADC93EB829CC9227ECD: “There is a tradition among the Dran of presenting their orphans with a necklace. Its purported purpose is to protect and comfort these sad creatures in the wake of their loss. Or so they say. Yet if we may be honest, which is a principle I take deeply, deeply to heart, then we must admit that its true aim is to quiet their incessant wailing that the other Dran may enjoy a good night’s sleep.”
871A5C194ABEBC6F044DE9B6277A4733: “There is an astronomical event in which a neutron star merges with a black hole. The result is a transient yet powerful explosion of energy, light, and precious elements. This phenomenon formed a key basis of the Drzyr’s calculations as to what might transpire upon entering Alepsis-Taura and how best to safeguard N’Erud against the resulting impact.”
AE7B01214AC1C31E9E2E95B8F29380D7: “There’s one thing all manner of Dran, critter, and monster share a fright of, and that thing is flame. My sweet Dran have learned to use it to their advantage, even before the creatures came. Oh, I sometimes wish they hadn’t, seeing what with where it got them.”
FC3452554D1EC0AFDA816CB1CF6FA22F: “They seem innocuous enough, but if those gloves could tell a tale, it would be one of gunpowder, death, and redemption.”
B9332F9A4A22D6FACE2D2F949E1D4D23: “Those feathery little devils are clever. Thieves, too. Blink and you’ll miss ‘em making off with something precious, and once they’ve got it, what’s theirs is theirs. Best to leave them be, dear.”
2B10633A4F113BE9251D36B17947CA0D: “Those who are easily cast the fool are my favorite sort of Fae...and there are pitiful few I don’t count amongst their numbers.”
6B5C316046B7EC7236C3C7A658AC6F60: “Though I have ever strived to keep my hands clean of blood—to as great an extent as is possible in my line of work, mind you—even I understand the necessity of sacrifice. Though I disagree with the Dran’s method of undertaking such endeavors in dismal sewers, I can at least appreciate the diligence it takes to do whatever must be done to see one’s schemes to fruition.”
63EED6124572F42273E9C4905F5E61AD: “Though he always ruled with a cruel fist of iron, the returned king was positively maniacal in his execution of vengeance. Yet it was not his manner of execution that was most fearsome, but rather how he punished those he chose to spare, and particularly his fondness for piked flesh. Thus my cleverly crafted disguise, if you must know.”
D1F1B608425A6232E61BA88F4EF63114: “Though many Fae challenged the king over the eons, only one ever commanded his attention and later his affections. According to the frivolous romantics of our time, she was said to be terrifying yet graceful in battle, and after every clash, the king felt moved to spare her. Magniloquent drivel, if you ask me. Not that I’ve ever read it.”
70E5D2E94C3326E2FB30ABB2FD3A25B7: “Though the despicable Dran somehow curried the king’s favor, to let them propagate would surely have brought the superior Fae to ruin. So, in an effort to prevent a catastrophe, Fae soldiers had no choice but to cull the vulgar masses for the greater good of all.”
014792474B26ED68C7440EBCE4E38637: “To consume. To destroy. To unmake. Utter and destined obliteration... The annulment of frail, derelict reality. In the absence of existence, all else is irrelevant. All is serenity.”
F3F25FA748E77B9721779384BD1C51A9: “To dally in the arcane is a fool’s errand. The key is to get as close to the powers of darkness as one can without allowing their meddling to sully your own reputation or prospects. A harsh fall awaits those who step too far down this path, though admittedly, there is much to be gained for those who manage to walk through the infernal flames without falling to ash.”
2DA619164D9B34CE137C3C88E0B4B303: “To hunt is to know its prey. To see what they see. Hear what they hear. But know them too well, and it may become prey itself.”
AED2C3204663339F823F08BCBC0985B4: “Traverse the depths both dark and light, / follow the current of the ember’s night.”
1E14FCB948E87D5B6CC11BA83D5EFF9D: “Turning whatever you can scrounge up into somethin’ tasty is kind of an art, ya know? The pot is my canvas and the meat is my paint. Just sit back and watch the master at work!”
CADA6BD94F1D40DAD56B69B73FF1C785: “Watching the Dran make attempts at the higher arts is like a bird skittering upon a dinner table as though it were an invited guest. It may eat from the same platter and drink from the same goblet as a Fae, but at the end of the day, its imitation must fall to the wayside as it inescapably returns to its feral routines along with the rest of its kind.”
EA8599FC4E0B0D1C7F59498433AFCA36: “We Fae adhere to a strict hierarchy. There are those above you and those below, and it is not the strongest nor proudest Fae who survive the longest—rather, the ones who know their place. Indeed, I am quite content to grovel to my betters if it means I outlive them in the end.”
D88D2BAF4009720EEF32DF8EB8222F57: “We Fae are not avaricious so much as we are possessive. We take what we desire, and once it’s in our possession, we’ve no mind to relinquish it from our claws. We are also vengeful by nature—a truly deadly combination, should one ever be foolish enough to steal from the Fae.”
7DB7161144586D187F7769A426BFD2BA: “Well, it may look like more duct tape than gun, but if you can point at the Root and take one down, that's all that matters in the end."
B6711EDB45EF594D99C3FEA93374EA30: “What does it take for a mere mortal to fell a goddess? I simply must know! For to vanquish those intolerable creatures whose boots are ever so firmly planted upon the backs of their intellectual superiors would be akin to becoming a god oneself...and I am very, very agreeable to the prospect of apotheosis.”
09086940436D66FE6ED76BAFCF6F5AE7: “What happened to the Dran who owned these? Why ever would you want to know that?”
85B90F504C82C57ADE72AFB7FFC877EB: “What is impossible to see, I perceive. What is impossible to fashion, I can forge. Such is my gift... and my curse.”
96458512452758E5EC2861B7A0A49CA6: “Whatever machine this was part of, I bet it misses this little fella. It only takes one missing piece to throw the whole thing out of whack. Keep that in mind next time something seems impossible—sometimes all you’re missing is one tiny, negligible cog.”
F8C382274143CCD8C597A4BAEB6693E6: “Whatever machine this was part of, I bet it misses this little fella. It only takes one missing piece to throw the whole thing out of whack. Keep that in mind next time something seems impossible—sometimes all you’re missing is one tiny, negligible cog.”
FE554E6D43C09D5704C748A524673A04: “Whatever machine this was part of, I bet it misses this little fella. It only takes one missing piece to throw the whole thing out of whack. Keep that in mind next time something seems impossible—sometimes all you’re missing is one tiny, negligible cog.”
45792C104A2E2079DD890384B2BF4927: “When allies wear it together, it fosters a sense of teamwork and encourages them to watch each other's backs out there. In a world as dangerous as this, having each other's support can make all the difference."
DDAAE71C4F2073505CE763BDF3825C87: “When humanity was barely scraping by an existence and everyone was gripped with a sense of fear and dread, there was Leto, tinkering away. Somehow, from the scant resources of that shattered wasteland, he found a way to engineer a suit of armor befitting the end of the world.”
9258BD734459E0B5D299778F5A9D5653: “When it comes to dealing with a crowd of Root bastards, nothing beats the satisfaction of lighting up the night sky with a well-placed pipe bomb.”
9B858FD641B3631E0332BA88D9FDE6DA: “When it comes to dealing with a crowd of Root bastards, nothing beats the satisfaction of lighting up the night sky with a well-placed pipe bomb.”
9F126990482ADDC5C1D85B8AD0B6E8DF: “When it comes to dealing with a crowd of Root bastards, nothing beats the satisfaction of lighting up the night sky with a well-placed pipe bomb.”
227267E8464EF3DA0DC363BCB66DB9F6: “When the Drzyr left their homeworld, they had to devise a new means of timekeeping. Because N’Erud does not orbit a star, the Seekers came up with N’Erudian Cycles. Observation: each world seems to have its own unique way of keeping time. I wonder how they compare to your own world.”
86B37DBB44385F2FFBA1768F4AF3377E: “When the whole world could disappear in the blink of an eye and most folks are getting their affairs in order or trying to find a glimmer of joy in the chaos, leave it to a tried-and-true scientist to focus on protecting their gray matter from the faintest threat of potential damage.”
07474C5D4CD76972361F90A26C5D32D9: “When you find yourself staring down a situation where even the air promises destruction, sometimes all that keeps you moving one foot in front of the other is the hunt.”
9C07247942B67508C9978682D53C7DF4: “Whether life beyond our own proved hostile, cordial, or yet infantile, the Drzyr would have received its discovery with tantamount jubilation. I ponder if it was not life, but the vindication of its existence we so desperately sought. To affirm that everything the Drzyr endured had been worth it; that in the end, it was not for nothing.”
246E407F461B127BF21FD39FD7667BC5: “While the Fae are so often accused of savagery—a description we quite embrace, as it were—even a cursory study of Dran culture reveals a propensity for torture offset by an abundance of penitence. This incongruity is one of the many bemusing things about those beasts.”
E1D96FF642D4E458796D40A96732A469: “Within her seat the Creator awaits / the Drzyr and their creations’ / cosmic embrace.”
40EA849C4E75BFCD3E2E48AC8DAC398B: “Yaesha wields beauty and danger in both hands. The Kin-Mother, like all mothers, bares her fangs to protect her young. The pestilence knows this well.”
C2D9C17941B459241ED37296A3AFF728: “You can tell a Dran’s character by his hands. Bruises, burns, needle pricks... Those are the hands of a humble and hard-working Dran. Soft and blemish free, stuffed in cozy gloves—don’t know a thing about the world, but probably thinks he does.”
554C5B684C553DEA17ADDAB93EB41AA1: “You can’t scratch a pup’s head with gloves and gauntlets in the way. Enough said.”
4A8F5FE148EBAA476C56FBBB9592831A: “You found this in the place with countless doors. Ford ventured there often, perhaps finding peace in its solitude or comfort in its nearly infinite possibilities.”
9FA4EBF6485F63E90FCD229DADE710C1: “You found this in the place with countless doors. Ford ventured there often, perhaps finding peace in its solitude or comfort in its nearly infinite possibilities.”
6AB2DA924FE739167A25EBA0B0542725: “You have served the Root well, but do not mistake this for favor. You sought power, and in doing so, betrayed your kind for a fleeting taste of what is inevitable—cessation.”
749B94A84455A4B0744CBBB5BFBF6A67: “You think a shoe’s simple ‘til you try to cobble one yourself. It takes skill and know-how, and without either of those, your cold feet would be bare. Don’t ever take anyone’s craft for granted, you hear me?”
4C8F941F42B05A749EF7628F2E693EE4: “You uncovered this on their earth. While it’s a bit terrifying to see what can happen to a world so much like ours, keep in mind that our earth would never have existed if the Root hadn’t come into being.”
5E609A674115BA89DA4A1F8FEF6EEDC4: “You uncovered this on their earth. While it’s a bit terrifying to see what can happen to a world so much like ours, keep in mind that our earth would never have existed if the Root hadn’t come into being.”
913D503944B30982C7696387B6A93286: “You unearthed this in the Ward. I saw you dig it up, not in my head, but with my own eyes. I’ve got a pretty good view of the shooting range from here.”
F1BF1D43409366449DDCAAA7FED8D04A: “You unearthed this in the Ward. I saw you dig it up, not in my head, but with my own eyes. I’ve got a pretty good view of the shooting range from here.”
32046698448F83207DCB359A937E430A: “You’d do well to remember that the clinking of spurs followed by the deafening burst of a bullet are the last sounds many a soul will ever hear.”
15205F044A09D53E00BE359D66691376:
“’We split the atom!’ they said. ‘We're about to put a man on the moon!’ they said. As if any of that gave us license to do the shit we did. Just 'cause you can doesn't mean you should.

I wish I'd said so back then. Even once.”

DeathQuotes.4: “After your death you will be what you were before your birth.” – Arthur Schopenhauer
DeathQuotes.7: “All that live must die, passing through nature to eternity.” – William Shakespeare
DeathQuotes.8: “Death does not concern us, because as long as we exist, death is not here. And when it does come, we no longer exist.” — Epicurus.
DeathQuotes.2: “Death may be the greatest of all human blessings.” – Socrates
DeathQuotes.6: “Live how we can, yet die we must.” – William Shakespeare
DeathQuotes.3: “No one can confidently say that he will still be living tomorrow.” – Euripides
DeathQuotes.5: “The boundaries which divide Life from Death are at best shadowy and vague. Who shall say where the one ends, and where the other begins?” – Edgar Allan Poe
DeathQuotes.1: “The greater the obstacle, the more glory in overcoming it.” – Molière
